title: If my kids and I ever get separated in public, I don’t just tell them to yell “Mum.” #familytravel
description:
If my kids and I ever get separated in public, I don’t just tell them to yell “Mum.”

Because in a crowded airport or theme park…
So many children could be shouting the exact same thing.

And in a real emergency, clarity matters.

So here is what I actually teach my kids before every trip.

Call out my full name. Loud and clear.
Not “Mum.” My actual name.

Go straight to a safe adult.
Police. Security. Staff with a name badge. Another parent with kids.

📲 Important: My kids wear @kidsflyer when we travel so they know to say: Please help me scan my shirt’s QR code to call my parents.

Stop and stay in one place.
Do not run around looking for me.

Use a strong voice.
Repeat clearly.

Know the simple script.
“My name is ____.”
“My mum’s name is ____.”
“I am lost.”

We practise this calmly at home.
Because when panic hits, children fall back on what they have rehearsed.

And I always tell them,
“If we ever get separated, I will come find you.”

But here is the honest truth.

Teaching safety rules is powerful.
But I did not want rules to be our only layer of protection.

We created KidsFlyer™ after experiencing that terrifying moment of losing sight of our child in public.

We realised something important.

Preparation should not rely on memory alone.

KidsFlyer™ is the world’s first safety travel outfit for kids.

Designed for busy airports.
Theme parks.
Hotels.
Crowded public events.

It is not just clothing.
It is a proactive safety system built into something your child is already wearing.

So if the unexpected happens, you are not relying only on what they remember to shout.
You have built in safety features working with you.

Before KidsFlyer™
I travelled with constant anxiety in the background.

After KidsFlyer™
I still teach the safety script.
But I feel equipped.
Prepared.
Calmer in crowded places.

If you are thinking,
“It probably will not happen to us.”

That is what every parent hopes.

But hope is not a strategy.
